summary: Valentino Papesso (1888–1944) was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Bologna from circa 1906 to 1911. He later served there as Docent of Sanskrit from circa 1925 to 1944.
Valeria Gazizova is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who completed her master's thesis at the University of Oslo. She studied under Hanna Havnevik and Per Kværne.

Valerie Hansen is a historian and sinologist who studied at Harvard and the University of Pennsylvania, also learning under Victor H. Mair. She held posts at East China Normal University and Yale University, where she became Professor of History in 1998.

Valerie Stoker works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, holding a post at Wright State University. She studied under traditional teachers D. Prahladachar and Krishnacharya Tammannacharya Pandurangi.

Valery Evgenyevich Krasnodembsky (1907–1942) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied at the Leningrad Oriental Institute. He worked as a naučnyj sotrudnik at his alma mater and the Institute of Ethnography, and taught at Saint Petersburg State University.
Vamana was an Indologist who studied under traditional teachers Keshava, Dattatreya Sastri Nigudkar, Virupaksha, and Vaidyanatha.
Vamanshastri Kinjawadekar was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under traditional teachers Dattatreya, Virupaksha, and Vaidyanatha.

Van Austin Harvey (1926–2021) was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Occidental College, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Yale. He held appointments at Princeton, SMU, the University of Pennsylvania, Clare Hall, Cambridge, and Stanford University.
Vandita Srivastava is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied at Banaras Hindu University, earning a BA (Hons.) between 2004 and 2007 and a PhD between 2010 and 2016.

Vans Kennedy (1784–1846) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. From 1817 to 1835, he served as judge-advocate-general in the Bombay Army, and he was an active member and later President (1831–1835) of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai.

Vasant Shinde is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who served as Professor and Professor of South Asian Archaeology at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested in 2006 and 2026).

Vasile Burlă (1840–1905) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the universities of Vienna and Graz. From circa 1872 to 1901, he served as a university lecturer in Classics at Alexandru Ioan Cuza University.

Vasilij Alekseevič Bogorodickij (1857–1941) was a linguist who studied at Kazan State University under Jan Niecisław Baudouin de Courtenay. He served as professor of Sanskrit and comparative grammar at Kazan State University and later taught at Kazan State Pedagogical University.

Vasilij Alekseevič Bogoslovskij (1932–1986) worked in Tibetology, sinology, and history and archaeology. After studying at Moscow State University, he served as naučnyj sotrudnik at the University of Chicago and worked at the Institute of China and Contemporary Asia.

Vasilij Ivanovič Smirnov (born 1898) was an Indologist who studied at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies and Saint Petersburg State University under Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov. He served as a docent at the Leningrad Oriental Institute from 1936 to 1937.

Vasilij Matveevič Beskrovnyj (1908–1978) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov at the Leningrad Oriental Institute. He held posts at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts, Leningrad Oriental Institute, Saint Petersburg State University, and Moscow State University.

Vasilij Vasil'evič Brodov (1912–1996) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at Moscow Institute of Philosophy, Literature and History. He taught at several Soviet institutions, including Moscow State University, and chaired philosophy at the All-Union Correspondence Civil Engineering Institute.

Vasily Mikhaylovich Alekseyev (1881–1951) was a sinologist who studied at St. Petersburg University and under Édouard Chavannes. He held long-term posts at Saint Petersburg State University, the Institute of Oriental Studies, and the National Library of Russia.

Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev (1818–1900) was a sinologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kazan State University under Erdmann, Kowalewski, and Archimandrite Daniil. He served as a professor at Kazan State University and Saint Petersburg State University.

Vasily Radlov (1837–1918) was a linguist and historian who studied at Berlin and Jena under Pott, Steinthal, and Schott. He served as director of the Asiatic Museum and the Peter the Great Museum of Anthropology and Ethnography (Kunstkamera).
